title: US Embassy Says Security Ramped Up Across Jordan After Deadly Karak Church Attack
excerpt: Gunmen fired on worshippers leaving a Coptic Orthodox church in Karak, killing at least two and wounding several including a child, as Jordan increased security at places of worship nationwide.
body:
• Gunmen attacked congregants leaving a Coptic Orthodox church in Karak, Jordan, on Friday; at least two worshippers were killed and several wounded, including a child in critical condition.
  • The US Embassy in Amman said Jordanian security presence has been increased around churches and places of worship nationwide, and urged US citizens to avoid areas with increased security activity.
  • Witnesses described shots striking worshippers at the church steps as families left the service, on the eve of a Coptic religious observance.
  • Indian nationals in Jordan — part of a large expatriate workforce across the Gulf and Levant — should follow local security advisories and avoid the affected areas of Karak.

Security has been stepped up around churches across Jordan after gunmen opened fire on worshippers leaving a Coptic Orthodox church in the southern city of Karak on Friday, killing at least two people and wounding several others, in an attack the US Embassy in Amman said had prompted a nationwide increase in security at places of worship.

The shooting happened at the Coptic Orthodox Church of Saint John the Beloved in Karak, about 87 miles south of Amman, as families left a service ahead of the night of the Apocalypse, a Coptic observance, according to The Hindu and The National. A medical source told The National that two fatalities and seven injuries had been received, with one child in critical condition, and that the wounded had undergone surgery for gunshot wounds. Police cordoned off the area around the church.

"We were leaving the church and going down the steps when we heard gunfire coming from the street. At first the shots were fired into the air, then they were directed at the people, right at the church steps."

— Eyewitness speaking to Sawt al Haq

What the embassy said

The US Embassy in Amman said it was aware of the shooting and of reports of assailants on foot in the area. "Out of an abundance of caution, security presence has been increased around churches and places of worship throughout Jordan," the embassy said, urging US citizens to monitor local media, avoid areas with increased security activity, and notify police of suspicious activity. No group had claimed responsibility in the initial reports, and Jordanian authorities had not publicly identified the attackers or a motive as of Saturday.

A city with a painful history

Karak carries a particular resonance for attacks on civilians in Jordan. In December 2016, Islamic State gunmen killed 19 people, including a Canadian tourist, in a series of attacks in and around the city and its Crusader-era castle. Friday's shooting at a Christian congregation — Copts in Jordan are a small minority, largely of Egyptian origin, and many had recently celebrated the Feast of Saint Demiana — revives questions about protection for minority places of worship across the region.

What to watch

Investigators will be pressed on whether the attackers acted alone, and churches across Jordan face decisions about services this weekend under the heightened security posture. Travellers and expatriates in Jordan, including the country's large Indian workforce in healthcare, construction and services, should follow embassy and local police guidance and avoid the Karak cordon area until authorities clear it.
